 Order

This i s first application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of the applicant who has been arrested relating to FIR/Crime No.33/2023 dated 14.02.2023 registered at Police Station Tamiya, District Chhindwara for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366-A, 376(2)(n), 376(3) and 506 of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is in custody since 23.02.2023 and trial will take considerable time to be concluded.
He further submits that applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.

He further submits that applicant is a permanent resident of district and is ready t o furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the conditions to be imposed Saleem Bharti vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31666978/
1 by the Court.

sentences.text: Upon these grounds, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes the bail application.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
The documents collected regarding the date of birth of prosecutrix show variance in that date.
According to Class-V mark-sheet, her date of birth was 10.08.2007 while her T.C. given after Class-I shows that her date of birth was recorded as 10.08.2005.
No explanation is there regarding variance in this date.
It appears that the age of the prosecutrix was more than 16 years at the time of incident.
She had accompanied with the applicant to various places and never complained to anyone.
She appears to be pregnant but case diary suggests that she never raised alarm against sexual advances made by the applicant.

Looking to the overall facts and circumstances of the case, this Court deems it proper to release the applicant on bail, therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, this application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of the trial.

It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of the Cr.P.C.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
(ANURADHA SHUKLA) JUDGE Nitesh Saleem Bharti vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31666978/
